title: Daily Market Digest: Friday, October 9, 2026 Session Wrap-up
subtitle: Markets closed for weekend - Reporting on Friday's session

sections.title: Market Pulse: US Stocks Close Strong Week

items.headline: US Equities Advance, Tech Sector Underperforms Amid AI Concerns
items.summary: U.S. stocks concluded a robust week with major indices posting gains on Friday, October 9, 2026. The S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq Composite all advanced, recovering from earlier volatility. While energy and real estate sectors showed strength, the technology sector lagged, notably impacted by concerns surrounding AI company revenues and Apple's reduced iPhone component orders. Consumer sentiment, however, saw a fifth consecutive monthly decline amid elevated gas prices and rising borrowing costs. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Humana Surges on Medicare Advantage Rating Upgrade
items.summary: Humana ($HUM) climbed 13% after the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) elevated its largest Medicare Advantage contract to 4 stars from 3.5, restoring quality bonus eligibility.

items.headline: Veea Gains on Nasdaq Compliance Announcement
items.summary: Veea ($VEEA) saw a significant pre-market increase of 28.42% to $3.87 after confirming its full compliance with Nasdaq's continued listing requirements.

items.headline: Moderna Rises After Rejoining Nasdaq-100
items.summary: Moderna ($MRNA) advanced 9.22% following its official re-entry into the Nasdaq-100 Index prior to the market open.

items.headline: Delta Air Lines Falls on Earnings Miss and Lowered Guidance
items.summary: Delta Air Lines ($DAL) shares declined 2.90% to $79.80 in pre-market trading after the airline missed earnings estimates for the first time in two years and cut its 2026 profit outlook, citing persistent high fuel costs.

items.headline: T-Mobile Slips on SpaceX Competition Concerns
items.summary: T-Mobile US ($TMUS) fell 9.54% following SpaceX's announcement of a spectrum acquisition agreement, which raised concerns about increased competition in the wireless carrier market.

items.headline: Apple Drops Amid Reports of Reduced iPhone Component Orders
items.summary: Apple ($AAPL) shares declined after reports indicated the company had reduced component orders for its upcoming iPhone series by 15-20% for October, signaling weaker demand.

items.headline: Energy and Real Estate Lead, Tech Lags Amid Sector Rotations
items.summary: Energy stocks emerged as the biggest gainers, with the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) advancing 3%. Real estate also performed strongly, up 1.88%, driven by wireless infrastructure companies benefiting from the SpaceX spectrum deal. Conversely, the technology sector was the worst performer, with the Information Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) declining 1.8%. The Communication Services sector also lagged, down 0.4%, due to competition concerns for traditional carriers following the SpaceX announcement.

items.headline: Jobless Claims Dip, Non-Farm Payrolls Miss Expectations
items.summary: The Labor Department reported that jobless claims fell by 2,000 to 197,000 for the week ending October 3. However, the September non-farm payroll report showed a gain of only 29,000 jobs, significantly below the anticipated 90,000. This weaker jobs data was viewed by some as potentially reducing the likelihood of another Fed rate hike in October.

items.headline: Consumer Sentiment Declines for Fifth Consecutive Month
items.summary: The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers revealed that consumer sentiment continued its downward trend in October, marking the fifth consecutive monthly decline. The index reached 46.3, a 13.6% drop year-over-year, largely attributed to elevated gas prices and rising borrowing costs.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season Approaches with High Expectations
items.summary: The third-quarter earnings season is set to kick off next week, with major U.S. banks slated to report. Analysts project S&P 500 companies to deliver robust year-over-year earnings per share growth of nearly 30%. The upcoming U.S. CPI report and corporate guidance will be crucial in assessing market direction and potential Federal Reserve actions.

items.headline: Oil Prices Retreat Slightly, Treasury Yields Remain Elevated
items.summary: Crude oil prices saw a slight retreat on Friday, with Brent crude down 1.2% to $103.01 a barrel and U.S. benchmark crude falling 0.9% to $90.69 a barrel. Despite this, energy prices remain elevated. The 10-year Treasury yield, after fluctuating, settled at 5.24%.
